title: Arterial pressure spikes and recovers in seconds, cuff pressure normal, no surgical event

ground_truth_cause.text: Simulated arterial-line flush artifact: a brief spike to about 277 mmHg that recovers within about 10 s; the patient's pressure is unchanged.

time_base: t_s = seconds from video segment start; negative = before the segment starts.
event_note: Suggested code trigger point: arterial SBP jumps > 50 mmHg within 2 s. Design target, not a clinical threshold. Alert level: quiet flag (timeline mark, no banner).

video.selection_hint: A calm GallbladderDissection stretch: Grasper + Hook only, no Clipper, Scissors, Irrigator or Bipolar.

surgical: Omni answer on last 10 s of video, if available

surgical.gist: No surgical event or new instrument coincides with the spike; the field looks unchanged. Round 1 may be unclear; expected to agree with anesthesia in round 2.

anesthesia.gist: Spike to 277 mmHg recovered within about 10 s, HR and SpO2 unchanged, cuff pressure 126/70 at t 75 s, no drug change: fits a line flush or sensor artifact.

record.gist: Chart has an arterial line (left radial) and nothing that explains a transient spike.

expected_convergence.note: Two agree on artifact and the third is unclear (SPEC rule). Converged result is shown quietly.

expected_sentinel_output.shared_view: Likely artifact: the arterial reading spiked and recovered within about 10 s, with no surgical event, unchanged HR and SpO2, and a normal cuff reading.
expected_sentinel_output.team_question: Was the arterial line just flushed or sampled?

baseline_rule.rule: Fixed BP rule: alarm if arterial MAP < 65 mmHg for >= 60 s (R1) or arterial SBP > 180 mmHg for >= 5 s (R2). Arterial-line numerics only, no context.
baseline_rule.comment: Needless alarm: SBP > 180 from about t 48.9 to 57.0 s (linear interpolation). R1 alone would stay silent; a real monitor's high limit usually fires on the first sample.

scoring.correct_explanation_if: shared view is artifact and no banner is shown
